headline: My garage conversion builder isn't communicating, what now?
articleBody:
One of the most frustrating things during a home renovation, especially a significant one like a garage conversion, is when your builder goes silent. Good communication is the backbone of any successful construction project, and a lack thereof can lead to misunderstandings, delays, cost overruns, and a whole lot of stress. You hired a professional to make your vision a reality, not to add to your worries. 

First, review your contract. It should outline expectations for communication, project timelines, and dispute resolution. Understanding what was agreed upon is your starting point for addressing the issue. Sometimes, just referring back to the contract can clarify things. 

Try to establish clear communication channels. If calls aren't working, switch to email or text so you have a written record. Send a concise message outlining your concerns and requesting a specific response or meeting. Be polite but firm about your need for updates. 

Document everything. Keep a log of all communications – dates, times, what was discussed, and any actions agreed upon. This includes photos of progress (or lack thereof) and any relevant project documents. This paper trail is invaluable if things escalate. 

If direct attempts fail, consider sending a formal written letter. Sometimes, a more official approach prompts action. If you're still hitting a wall and the project is stalling, it might be time to seek advice from a construction consultant or an attorney specializing in construction law – though that's usually a last resort. 

To avoid this altogether, choose a builder known for clear communication from the start. Cali View Builders prides itself on transparent, direct communication, ensuring you're always in the loop.
